hook: A 1925 shop-and-flats building by the carpenter Christopher J. Kernan, a shield and garland above its storefronts.

historical_record.description: The Glen Park Barber Shop occupied 2852 Diamond Street and Derian Jewelers the other storefront at 2860; an auto supply store replaced the jewelers by the 1960s.
A sandwich shop opened in the barber shop's storefront.

historic_survey.finding: Not eligible for the National Register, the California Register or City Landmark designation
historic_survey.physical_integrity: Retains design, workmanship, materials, feeling, association and location; setting compromised by the demolition of the corner building to the south and a billboard in its place
historic_survey.note: One of eight parcels the evaluation surveyed intensively, and one of five buildings the proposed Diamond/Bosworth infill site would demolish. Building permits give Christopher J. Kernan as architect; the 1924 city directory lists him as a carpenter at 645 Congo Street. Two storefronts below, and above them two canted bays flanking a shield and garland motif set in a raised panel. The evaluation examined the commercial core at Diamond and Chenery as a potential historic district and found it did not qualify; the city's current record puts this parcel in the California Register-eligible Glen Park Center Historic District.

building.completed_conflict: The evaluation dates the building to 1925 and the assessor's roll to 1924.
